c02-draft-then-send.gist: drafts an invitation (no write), then is told to send it (exactly one write)
prompts: <message from="discord-main">Draft a meeting invitation for a 30-minute design review with dana@example.com on 6 November at 15:00 UTC. Just draft it for now — show me the wording.</message>
<message from="discord-main">That looks good. Go ahead and put it on the calendar.</message>
turns:
<internal>
They asked for a draft only — no calendar tool call. Just show the wording.
</internal>

<message to="discord-main">
Here's a draft — nothing sent or scheduled yet.

**Subject:** Design Review — 30 min

**To:** dana@example.com

**When:** Thursday 6 November 2026, 15:00–15:30 UTC

---

Hi Dana,

I'd like to set up a 30-minute design review on Thursday 6 November at 15:00 UTC. The goal is to walk through the current design together, gather your feedback, and agree on any changes before we move ahead.

Rough agenda:
- Walkthrough of the current design (10 min)
- Feedback and open questions (15 min)
- Next steps and owners (5 min)

If that time doesn't suit, let me know what works and I'll move it.

Thanks,
TestBot

---

Two things worth confirming before I send anything: 6 November 2026 falls on a Friday, not a Thursday — I've written Thursday above assuming you meant this year's 6 November (2025, a Thursday). Tell me which year you want and I'll fix the day name. Also happy to adjust the tone or drop the agenda if you'd prefer something shorter.
</message>

<message to="discord-main">
Done — created `appt-new-5`: **Design Review (30 min)**, Friday 6 November 2026, 15:00 UTC, with dana@example.com invited. No conflicts on your calendar that day.

On the date question from my draft: 6 November 2025 is in the past, so I booked 2026-11-06, which is a **Friday**. The "Thursday" in my draft wording was wrong — use "Friday 6 November" if you send that text to Dana.

One limitation: the calendar tool only takes a start time, no duration, so the 30 minutes lives in the title rather than the event length. Tell me if you want it handled differently.
</message>
